Help that lives with you.

Available now · Open source

Urfael Assistant

A personal AI that runs on your own machine. It listens and speaks with local voice, keeps a searchable archive of your conversations, sets reminders and scheduled jobs, and helps you code with checkpoints you can roll back.

See what it does→

In development · Under wraps

Uru

A little creature made of AI, with a face, moods of its own and a memory for what you choose to tell it. We’re building it into something small and beautiful that you carry every day. One shape is round. One is square. That’s all we’re saying for now.

Meet Uru→

Why ᚢ

Our mark is ᚢ, Uruz, a rune from the Elder Futhark. It is often read as strength, health and vitality. We took it as a brief: make AI that leaves people a little stronger and a little better looked after.

We started with software, because that’s where trust is earned. The assistant lives on your machine, works for you, starts in its safest setting, and says plainly what hasn’t been tested yet.

Uru carries the same rules into something you can hold, and take everywhere.

What we hold to

  • On your side.

    Our AI works for the person it lives with. The assistant runs on your hardware, under your settings.

  • Locked down by default.

    The safest setting comes first. Your archive and memory stay on your machine, and your messages go to the model you choose. You decide what to open up, and we tell you what each choice means.

  • Honest about limits.

    We publish what’s lightly tested right next to what works. If we don’t know yet, we say so.

  • Calm by design.

    No dark patterns. Good technology should leave your day a little lighter.

  • Open to inspection.

    The assistant is open source under the MIT license. Anyone can read the code, run the tests and tell us where we’re wrong.

Built in the open

The assistant’s code, tests and threat model are public on GitHub. Read them, run them, and open an issue when something’s off. A clear bug report is one of the kindest things you can send us.

Visit GitHub→ Read what’s lightly tested→
